author: Balder13946731
text:
最近看各家大厂都在疯狂吹自家的Agent，画饼说以后能帮用户全自动买机票、找折扣。我觉得这帮人没安好心。

大家好像都没仔细想过，等这玩意儿真在C端普及了，整个消费市场会彻底异化成一个高频交易的暗池（Dark Pool）。

当你放权让Agent去下单时，本质上就是你的AI跟商家的定价AI在后台直接接火。你的模型想靠回测历史数据抠出底价，对方的模型瞬间扫完你的资产画像和行程急迫度，毫秒级算出你的最高榨取空间。这就跟现在华尔街的量化机构神仙打架一模一样，两边在暗处互相抛单、疯狂博弈。

最荒谬的是，不管你的Agent最终帮你砍下多少钱，也不管商家的Agent多榨出了多少溢价，这中间高频博弈烧掉的庞大算力，最后全都会变成打给云巨头和老黄的通道费。相当于买卖双方在盘口厮杀得头破血流，最后全去给交易所交了算力印花税

author: Balder13946731
text:
Everyone's waiting to see AI turn up in the electricity bill. It'll turn up in the price of a laptop first.

An HBM bit eats roughly three times the wafer capacity of a plain DRAM bit, and Hynix and Samsung have spent two years converting lines over to make them, so commodity DRAM supply has been shrinking right into the best demand year memory has ever had. You haven't felt it because PCs and phones buy on contract — that repricing lands a couple of quarters late, inside somebody's gross margin. Dell's, for one. Memory is a real chunk of the BOM there, the operating margin is mid single digits, and the guy outbidding them for the same wafer is financing his cluster with money that doesn't care what it costs. There isn't much of a negotiation in that.

Cleanest money in AI is still memory. Hynix helped build this shortage and is selling into it.

我一直觉得这事的后果被低估了：整条AI链上最不可替代的一环，偏偏是唯一一个不以利润最大化为目标的玩家。它不往上加价，省下的那块钱就留在了ASML和台积电的毛利里，最后变成英伟达的卡价和你看到的那些财报。

假设哪天这个基金会想开了，决定像正常公司那样收租——这条链上每一家的毛利都得重算一遍。

**板块**：全日呈典型的「软件靠稳、硬件挫」格局。软件及平台股造好，甲骨文（ ORCL ）急升4.23%，为观察股之首；Meta（ META ）升2.63%，Salesforce（ CRM ）升1.75%，IBM（ IBM ）升1.66%。支付股逆市走强，Visa（ V ）升1.74%，万事达（ MA ）升1.63%。消费及汽车亦有承接，通用汽车（ GM ）升1.98%，劳氏（ LOW ）升1.71%。另一边，半导体设备与存储股领跌，应用材料（ AMAT ）重挫6.69%，美光（ MU ）跌3.62%，SK海力士相关（ SKHY ）跌3.19%；网络设备股 Arista（ ANET ）跌3.02%，AI云服务商 CoreWeave（ CRWV ）跌3.05%。投机性板块失守，太空及卫星概念最弱，AST SpaceMobile（ ASTS ）暴跌8.54%，SPCX 跌4.21%；量子计算股同步急泻，IonQ（ IONQ ）跌4.25%，Rigetti（ RGTI ）跌3.55%。工业股亦见回吐，卡特彼勒（ CAT ）跌3.33%。

**焦点**：市场对 AI 这条链的定价正在分化。 ORCL 、 META 、 CRM 升，而 AMAT 、 MU 、 ANET 、 CRWV 同日跌——资金买的是手握应用与现金流的一端，卖的是依赖资本开支落地的另一端。 AMD 逆势升1.90%，Semtech（ SMTC ）升2.67%，说明沽压并非笼罩整个半导体板块，而是直指存储与设备。消息面上，亚马逊将 META 的 AI 购物代理挡在站外，一端涉及广告位的存续，一端涉及电商闭环的缺口；此事与当日涨跌幅并无直接对应，仅作题材观察。此外，国际货币基金组织最新报告将「AI市场回调」与战争、债务并列为全球风险，与设备及存储链的持续沽压构成同一条叙事线。

**小结**：全日属轻微调整市，但市宽与投机板块的伤势远重于指数。 SPY 守于778点一线，是大市未转弱的第一道证明； QQQ 743.57点与 DIA 516.21点同日跌0.33%，科网未能跑出；最值得跟的是 IWM 的276.71点——小型股跌0.43%，若此位失守，当日这种「指数平收、内部走弱」的组合便不易维持。半导体设备与存储链能否在 AMAT 大挫后靠稳，仍是下一步大市方向的关键参照。

Not all neoclouds are created the same way not all neocloud capacity is worth the same, and this chart shows it.

Every gigawatt Nebius signs away in a long-term hosting deal brings in roughly $20-25B. 

The same gigawatt sold short-term on its own platform brings in $40-50B. Same power, same data center, about double the revenue.

Serverless inference is the purest version of that. 

Instead of renting a cluster for five years, customers pay per token for exactly what they use, while Nebius runs the hardware, the software and the optimization in between.

Why I think it's the next big leg for 
$NBIS
:

+ Training is lumpy and driven by a few giant customers. Inference is every company shipping an AI product, every single day.
+ Usage-based pricing scales with adoption. More agents means more tokens, which means more revenue from the same gigawatt.
+ The software is the moat. Uptime guarantees, speculative decoding and auto-scaling are hard to copy for someone who's just renting out racks.
+ It spreads revenue across thousands of customers instead of a couple of hyperscalers.

The big contracts pay for the build but inference is where the money is.

Bet on the companies that are pushing for more server-less inference.

Cerebras is trading more than 50% below where it opened on its first day, and I just couldn’t pass up this opportunity.

UBS sees revenue going ~25x by 2030 at 46% margins, and the stock trades at about 20x 2028 earnings. 

I keep saying this: the growth story for AI is inference.

Training a model is a big upfront project. Running it, every time someone asks a question or an agent takes a step, is a bill that never stops, and the agentic shift makes that bill much bigger. A single agent task can fire off dozens of model calls, and every one of them waits on the one before it. A few seconds of waiting per call turns into minutes per task.

Cerebras attacks that wait directly. 

A GPU keeps the model’s weights in HBM next to the chip and has to pull them across for every token it generates. Cerebras builds one chip out of an entire silicon wafer, about 46,000 mm² and 4 trillion transistors against roughly 1,600 mm² and 208 billion for NVIDIA’s two-die B200, and keeps 44GB of memory on the wafer itself. 

Less waiting on memory means more tokens per second for each user, which is exactly what an agent stuck in a loop of model calls needs.

GPUs are the best general-purpose factory ever built. 

Cerebras is a specialist tool for one job, fast inference, and that’s one of the fastest-growing jobs in AI.

The stock is still richly priced and could go lower, but this is a long bet I’m willing to take.
